    Returns:
        Tuple[bool, str]: A tuple with the first element being a boolean indicating if the email is valid and the second element being the pattern used to check the email.
    """

    # It allows alphanumeric characters, '.', '_', '%', '+', and '-'.
    # This pattern is designed to prevent leading/trailing special characters and consecutive special characters,
    # while still being permissive for common special characters used in local parts.
    # Examples: 'user.name', 'user_name', 'user+tag', 'user-name', 'user%name' are valid.
    # '.user', 'user.', 'user..name', 'user--name' are invalid by this pattern.
    # This pattern ensures the local part starts and ends with an alphanumeric character,
    # and any special characters (._%+- ) are always followed by an alphanumeric character.
    local_part_pattern = r"[a-zA-Z0-9]+(?:[._%+-][a-zA-Z0-9]+)*"

    # Regex for a single domain label (e.g., 'def', 'ghi', 'com').
    # A label must start and end with an alphanumeric character.
    # Hyphens are allowed internally but not at the beginning or end of a label.
    # The maximum length of a domain label is 63 characters (RFC 1035).
    # This pattern allows single-character labels (e.g., 'a.b.com').
    # It matches a character, then optionally a sequence of 0-61 chars (alphanumeric or hyphen)
    # followed by another alphanumeric character. This covers 1 to 63 characters.
    domain_label_pattern = r"[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?"

    # Regex for the Top-Level Domain (TLD), e.g., 'uk', 'com', 'net', 'museum'.

    # This pattern ensures at least two characters and adheres to domain label rules.
    # Example: 'com', 'uk', 'museum', 'xn--fiqs8s' (for IDNs, though this pattern is more for standard ASCII).
    # The pattern `[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])` ensures at least two characters
    # because the `(?:...)` group is not optional.
    tld_pattern = r"[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])"

    # Combine the parts into the full email regex pattern.
    # ^                                  # Asserts the start of the string.
    # {local_part_pattern}               # Matches the local part (e.g., 'abc.123').
    # @                                  # Matches the literal '@' separator.
    # {domain_label_pattern}             # Matches the first domain label (e.g., 'def').
    # (?:                                # Non-capturing group for subsequent domain labels.
    #   \.                               # Matches a literal dot separator.
    #   {domain_label_pattern}           # Matches a subsequent domain label (e.g., 'ghi', 'com').
    # )*                                 # Allows zero or more subsequent domain labels.
    # \.                                 # Matches the literal dot separator before the TLD.
    # {tld_pattern}                      # Matches the Top-Level Domain (e.g., 'uk').
    # $                                  # Asserts the end of the string.
    email_pattern = rf"^{local_part_pattern}@{domain_label_pattern}(?:\.{domain_label_pattern})*\.{tld_pattern}$"

    # Use re.fullmatch to ensure the entire string matches the pattern.
    is_valid = bool(re.fullmatch(email_pattern, email))

    return is_valid, email_pattern
